text:
sophie: quick heads-up — sirius14b (int4) canary hit OOMs on a few 512-token interactive requests from the analytics suite this morning
aj: saw that, got an alert from deploy-bot: `oom: allocation failed: size=...` on rtx-pool-7
kai: logs? stacktrace?
sophie: paste: ```runtime: out of memory
2026-03-19T08:12:02Z serve: alloc 1.2GiB failed for kv-cache
trace: malloc failed at serve/kv/alloc.go:87
```
eli: repro steps? is it max_new_tokens or batching window?
sophie: reproduces locally with prompt len ~120 + max_new_tokens=384 under high QPS batch_mode=continuous
aj: looks like fragmentation — after a few long sessions memory doesn't compact; jemalloc stats show arena_growth at 3.2G
kai: on int4 we reduced weight footprint, but KV cache and activations still dominate. suspect prefetch + large max_new_tokens is the trigger
ops: can we throttle max_new_tokens at routing layer for canary? policy exists per-model yes/no
eli: we can set a temporary route override: default.max_new_tokens = 128 for sirius14b-canary and keep full on dedicated until fix
sophie: +1 do that, also reduce batch_max_tokens from 2048->1024 to avoid big aggregations
aj: note: continuous batching window currently spikes when latency < 50ms, maybe that policy too aggressive for int4 memory patterns
kai: quick mitigation patch: limit batching to 8 concurrent requests for sirius14b and enable kv-prefetch=false for short sessions. will bake a canary in ~20m
sophie: sounds good. also add an alloc-compaction step in runtime on eviction (heuristic: compact after >10% fragmentation) — long-term fix
eli: for immediate rollbacks: deploy-bot can auto-fallback to sirius14b-fp16 variant if OOM rate >0.5% over 5m. set that trigger?
ops: set fallback trigger now, done. routing shows active canary weight 12%
sophie: running evals for quality after int4->fp16 fallbacks to sanity-check outputs (some tokenization differences expected)
aj: heads-up for billing: fallback to fp16 will increase token cost ~1.9x for these sessions
kai: experiment notes: suspected root cause was allocator fragmentation + large per-request kv reservation when max_new_tokens high. patch in branch: `sirius/allocator/compact-on-evict` — adds explicit `malloc_trim()` call and reduces per-request kv-reserve from 1.0x->0.7x
sophie: can we also reduce default max_new_tokens for v1 runtime models that are int4-quantized? maybe a global opt-in flag per-quant profile
eli: agreed. propose: quant-profile=int4 -> recommended.max_new_tokens=128, recommended.batch_tokens=1024 in Optimize suggestions
aj: after canary changes and routing fallback, we saw OOM count drop to 0 in the last 10m on canary nodes
sophie: nice. follow-ups: 1) merge allocator patch 2) add optimize suggestion 3) update onboarding doc to warn about int4 kv-prefetch memory 4) add a smoketest with repeated long prompts
ops: created tickets: INF-988 (allocator patch), INF-989 (onboard doc), INF-990 (routing default override).
deploy-bot: deploy sirius14b-canary patch scheduled to kube/rtx-pool in 15m :rocket:
kai: i'll monitor memmaps and jemalloc metrics, will ping if fragmentation creeps back
sophie: thanks all. @aj please post short postmortem if we hit rollback, otherwise update the canary notes when patch lands :thumbsup:
